- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Before the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989, East Berlin had a strict socialist realism style in art and functionalist architecture, while West Berlin had modernist and post-modernist styles.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Berlin Wall became a symbol and subject of artistic expression, with graffiti, murals, and installations on both sides.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In West Berlin, artists used the wall for political and social commentary, while East Berlin artists challenged state-imposed styles through underground movements.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] After the Wall's fall, there was a mix of architectural styles and a boom in public art, galleries, and performance spaces.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Today, Berlin is a hub for contemporary art and architecture, influenced by its divided past.
